newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower on harvest and yield reports.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower on harvest and yield reports.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower, weighed down by harvest pressure including persistent reports of better-than-expected yields, traders said.
New crop July set a fresh 4-1/2-month low when it touched a session low of $3.36 a bushel, the lowest price since February 7.
Meteorologists Thursday said weather would remain conducive for combining through Saturday, when rain is expected to move into the area.

Cash sources early Thursday said up to 85-bushel-per-acre yields were reported in the southern Kansas hard red winter wheat region and better-than-expected yields were noted in the areas that were hit by an April freeze.
Also, dealers in Arkansas Wednesday said soft red winter wheat yields were very good.
Commercial selling again was featured with Cargill Inc selling 3.5 million bushels of July, traders said. LIT America bought 2.5 million bushels of July, traders said.
Wheat futures closed 3-3/4 cents per bushel lower to 1-1/2 higher, with July down 1-3/4 at $3.37 a bushel.
The market dropped despite some early ideas that support might surface from the export sector.

There was news Pakistan June 25 would seek 500,000 tonnes of optional-origin wheat and USDA's weekly export sales report was supportive. USDA Thursday said during the week ended June 12 U.S. net export sales of wheat totalled 531,600 tonnes, above expectations for 100,000 to 200,000 tonnes.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 21,000 contracts, above the 20,038 traded Wednesday.
In wheat options, FIMAT Futures sold 100 July $3.40 puts at five cents, Refco Inc sold 100 July $3.40 puts at five cents and sold 100 September $3.40 puts at 10-3/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 8,000 contracts, below the 9,075 traded Wednesday.
